Michael Saylor: MSCI Is Biased Against Digital Assets

On October 14, 2026, Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor said in a Bloomberg interview that MSCI is biased against digital assets, recognizing oil, land, and machinery as capital while refusing to recognize Bitcoin. He emphasized that, like banks and insurance companies, Strategy holds assets and sells financial products—specifically digital credit—and is therefore an operating company. If holding financial assets were grounds for exclusion from an index, the same logic should apply to banks and insurance companies. He also said the amount of capital affected by MSCI’s decision is limited and would have little impact on the company. — link

OCC Finalizes First GENIUS Act Rule: No Safe Harbor for Existing Stablecoin Rewards

The OCC has issued its first final rule implementing the GENIUS Act, covering stablecoin issuance, custody, and third-party partnerships, effective January 18, 2027. Existing yield and rewards programs receive no automatic grandfathering or safe harbor; compliance will be assessed case by case.

The act prohibits issuers from paying yield solely for holding, using, or retaining stablecoins, but does not ban all third-party rewards. The OCC said rewards based at least partly on other factors may fall outside the prohibition. The implications for programs offered by Coinbase, PayPal, and Kraken remain uncertain. — link
